## 固定收益開篇論點

6月18日，荷莫茲海峽開始恢復實體油氣運輸，風險資產上漲；在聯準會鷹派重新定價後，投資人轉而買進中長天期美債，公債反彈主要集中在政策敏感的前端之外。2年期殖利率小跌0.6個基點至4.18%，幾乎保留前一日全部升幅；5年期下降3個基點至4.233%，10年期與30年期均下降3.4個基點，分別收在4.455%與4.899%。

這波不均衡的漲勢延續Kevin Warsh首度以聯準會主席身分主持會議後形成的殖利率曲線趨平。2年與10年期利差再收窄2.8個基點至27.5個基點，全週累計趨平12.4個基點；2年與30年期利差則壓縮至71.9個基點。市場一方面認為近期政策收緊的機率已大幅上升，另一方面相信較嚴格的政策配合未來能源成本下降，有助於抑制較長期的通膨。

10年期殖利率的變動結構，並不像名目殖利率下跌本身所顯示的那麼偏向通膨降溫。10年期實質殖利率下降3.9個基點至2.181%，損益兩平通膨率反而上升0.5個基點至2.274%。週四對長天期債券的買盤，主要來自經通膨調整後殖利率下降，而非長期通膨補償再次下滑。相較之下，過去一個月損益兩平通膨率下降22.4個基點，實質殖利率則上升9.1個基點。

能源實體供應情勢改善有利長天期美債，卻未使原油價格全面下跌。美國與伊朗的臨時協議生效後，載有近1,000萬桶石油或液化天然氣的船舶已駛出或進入荷莫茲海峽。WTI下跌0.25%至每桶$76.60，布蘭特原油則上漲0.38%至$79.85；兩者全週仍下跌超過11%，近一個月跌幅接近29%。船運恢復降低海峽長期完全封鎖的機率，但當日油價漲跌互見，顯示市場仍不確定正常運量及受損供應基礎設施能以多快速度恢復。

美國數據並未削弱聯準會對通膨的警戒。初領失業救濟金人數降至22.6萬人，接近預期；費城聯準銀行製造業指數反彈至10.3，支付價格指數升至53.2。不過，續領失業救濟金人數增至181萬人，勞動市場仍可見部分降溫跡象。整體數據足以延續市場對7月或9月升息的討論，卻未強到引發美債又一輪全面拋售。

風險資產將荷莫茲海峽恢復通行視為更迫切的發展。標普500指數上漲1.08%，那斯達克100指數上漲2.48%，半導體指數大漲6.42%，VIX則下跌11.06%至16.40。隨著美國利率預期繼續高於多個其他經濟體，美元指數上漲0.76%；黃金期貨下跌3.09%至$4,224.10。投資級、高收益及新興市場債券基金亦小幅走高。因此，收盤走勢並非避險行情：投資人將能源供應改善與聯準會近期更嚴格的政策反應區分看待，長天期美債、股票及信用債基金價格同步上漲。

## 美債反彈，前端仍保持警戒

美債回升並未明顯扭轉殖利率曲線所反映的核心政策訊息。Warsh首度主持會議前，交換市場認為7月升息的機率幾乎為零；至週四，市場隱含7月28日至29日會議升息25個基點的機率已接近五成，並已完全反映10月前升息一次。2年期殖利率雖小幅回落，全週仍上升11.7個基點；10年期略低於一週前，30年期則下降5.7個基點。

聯邦基金期貨交易顯示，這次重新定價包含大量新增風險部位，不只是市場清淡造成的價格波動。在用以表達7月升息預期的市場區段，成交量超過50萬口，約為20日均量的4倍，並創下紀錄。8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量增加6.7萬口，相當於該期限既有部位約15%。由於這些合約在9月會議前到期，交易焦點直接集中於7月。

市場也在解除押注降息的部位。2026年6月擔保隔夜融資利率期貨未平倉量減少9萬口。聯邦基金期貨總未平倉量仍低於1年平均，但8月新增部位與偏鴿派SOFR部位減少同時出現，顯示市場對Warsh的反應並非僅止於現券美債的一日調整。

新任主席並未明示政策行動時點；他偏好減少前瞻指引，反而使每一項通膨、就業與經濟活動數據更加重要，尤其是在曲線前端。即使聯準會沒有立即升息，曲線仍可能趨平：強勁的月度數據可能使緊縮時點提前，增加短天期債券風險；若市場相信聯準會會在通膨預期進一步失穩前採取行動，長天期債券則可望受益。

高盛副董事長、前達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Rob Kaplan也支持這種有條件的解讀。他表示，若通膨屆時仍未降溫，官員可能需要在9月或秋季升息。Kaplan並指出，政策調整很少只是單次行動，因此9月升息後，可能再升息一至兩次。不過，他也提出重要保留：最新預測可能尚未充分納入美國與伊朗的協議及航運路線重啟，聯準會9月更新預測時，通膨展望仍有改善空間。

週四經濟數據也呈現這種拉鋸。截至6月13日當週，初領失業救濟金人數減少4,000人至22.6萬人，市場預期為22.5萬人；前一週數字由22.9萬人上修至23萬人。新增裁員仍然有限，並未出現可能迫使聯準會忽略通膨的快速惡化。

較不利的勞動訊號出現在持續性指標。初領失業救濟金人數4週平均由修正後的21.925萬人升至22.325萬人，創去年12月以來新高。截至6月6日當週，續領人數增加2.4萬人至181萬人，前值由179.5萬人下修至178.6萬人；投保失業率維持1.2%。儘管最新新增申請人數仍低，就業與重新就業可能正變得更加困難。

製造業則釋出較強的成長訊號，但成本面並不舒服。費城聯準銀行6月一般經濟活動指數由負0.4反彈至10.3，略高於9.8至10.0的預期區間。新訂單由負1.7躍升至27.3，出貨由4.9升至14.9，就業則由負2.8回到正值7.9。訂單、產出與就業全面改善，顯示復甦並非只有整體指數反彈。

價格壓力同時增強。支付價格指數由47.9升至53.2，收取價格指數則由26.3降至20.3。製造商仍保持樂觀：未來一般經濟活動指數為50.2，僅略低於53.2；預期資本支出由30.9增至41.2。因此，這份報告反映的是成長與投入成本同步上升，而非明確的通膨降溫訊號。

美債供給另對實質利率結構形成考驗。財政部增額發行$240億5年期抗通膨債券，得標實質殖利率為1.955%，遠高於4月$260億新券發行時的1.367%。投標倍數由2.57升至2.61；間接投標人取得獲接受競標的68.59%，直接投標人取得27.99%，一級交易商僅承接3.43%，低於4月的8.48%。

得標實質殖利率較4月大幅提高，主要反映其間市場水準已顯著改變。不過，需求數據顯示投資人以略高的投標倍數及更大的最終投資人合計占比吸收這次增額發行。該券票息為1.250%，2031年4月15日到期，並於6月30日交割。

抗通膨債券現貨市場的交易格外熱絡。FINRA記錄的TIPS面額交易量為$478億，較前一交易日增加114.3%。剩餘期限不超過5年的TIPS交易量增加130.1%至$313億，其中最新券占69.3%。這些數據無法判定投資人交易方向，但活動集中於標售所在期限，證實此次增額發行適逢市場參與度顯著提高。

國庫券標售結果則較分歧。財政部$700億4週期國庫券的得標殖利率為3.580%，低於一週前的3.595%；投標倍數由3.13降至2.99，但間接投標占比升至72.30%，交易商承接占比降至24.46%。$750億8週期國庫券的得標殖利率則由3.610%升至3.640%，投標倍數由2.94降至2.57；間接投標占比降至51.49%，交易商承接44.56%，高於前次的28.14%。兩者均於6月23日交割，但8週期標售分配較弱，顯示相鄰期限的前端現金需求並不一致。

## 英國按兵不動，全球政策路徑分歧

英格蘭銀行將政策利率維持在3.75%，但即使油價已大幅回落，7比2的表決結果仍保留實質升息風險。首席經濟學家Huw Pill與外部委員Megan Greene主張立即升息25個基點至4%。4月時只有Pill持不同意見，因此鷹派少數擴大仍具重要性，儘管多數委員選擇等待。

英格蘭銀行將第4季通膨高點預測由3.6%下修至3.25%，反映未來能源成本前景改善。油價已從戰時高點每桶$108降至$80以下；5月消費者物價通膨為2.8%，低於央行預測的3.3%。官員也認為需求與勞動市場疲弱將限制第二輪效應。

國內經濟活動數據支持耐心等待。自2月伊朗戰爭爆發以來，英國已流失6.4萬個工作機會；民營部門不含獎金的薪資增幅降至5年來最低，4月GDP萎縮0.1%。英格蘭銀行估計第1季基礎成長率僅0.2%，預期第2季亦為相近速度。多數貨幣政策委員會成員認為，衝突爆發以來金融條件收緊，已對通膨提供一定防護。

維持利率不代表能源衝擊已經結束。總裁Andrew Bailey表示油價下跌令人鼓舞，但仍高於戰前水準，中東基礎設施受損程度也仍待評估。多數委員表示，若價格壓力增強，央行應採取有力對策；Greene則主張，在有證據顯示較大的第二輪效應並未出現之前，仍應預先防範。

市場略微下調英格蘭銀行進一步緊縮的預期，但仍完全反映今年升息25個基點一次，並反映約30%的第二次升息機率。英鎊兌美元下跌約0.5%至$1.3225，創4月初以來最低。這項反應同時反映較低的通膨預測，以及Warsh首度主持會議後美國政策利差擴大。

歐元區對升息的討論更為明確。歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，中性利率估計區間上緣已由2.25%升至2.5%。在6月11日升息後，存款利率為2.25%；依此判斷，再升息25個基點未必會使政策明確進入限制性區域。

Lane將中東事件描述為規模中等、持續程度中等的衝擊，影響小於俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭後的供應中斷，但仍可能使通膨長期高於目標。他預期，即使油價下跌，先前累積的能源衝擊仍會推高食品、商品及服務價格。

其他歐洲央行官員指出，影響範圍已在擴大。Jose Luis Escrivá表示，能源成本正反映於核心通膨，服務、運輸及食品尤其明顯。他強調薪資的第二輪效應尚未出現，但不能據此假設未來也不會發生。Martin Kocher同樣表示，儘管已達成臨時和平協議，消費者物價仍會在一段時間內維持高檔，歐洲央行也已準備採取行動。

西班牙凸顯歐元區內的價格壓力。西班牙央行將2026年通膨預測上調至3.6%，較3月預測高0.6個百分點，理由包括能源、非能源工業產品、服務，以及燃料成本上升的部分轉嫁；2027年預測亦小幅上調至2.6%。其成長預測仍遠強於整體歐元區，今年為2.3%、明年為1.7%，使西班牙同時面對較強經濟活動與更持久的通膨。

亞洲央行則更直接面對貨幣貶值與輸入性通膨。印尼央行將BI利率上調25個基點至5.75%，這是約一個月內第三度升息，也是今年累計緊縮100個基點的最新一步。總裁Perry Warjiyo表示，央行將繼續積極行動以支撐印尼盾。

決策公布後，印尼盾收盤升值0.2%，印尼10年期公債殖利率則上升15個基點，為逾一週最大升幅。自7月起，至少$1萬的外幣交易必須具備實質交易背景，門檻低於今年稍早的$10萬。印尼央行估計，新規將使具有實質交易文件支持的外匯交易占比升至98.1%。

這輪緊縮主要由匯率與資本流動推動，而非當前整體通膨；整體通膨預料仍處於央行1.5%至3.5%的目標區間。不過，食品與能源成本、聖嬰現象可能造成的干擾，以及印尼盾走弱的滯後影響，仍構成上行風險。聯準會可能升息則使美元資產更具競爭力，並提高穩定匯率的成本，進一步加重壓力。

菲律賓中央銀行也將目標附買回利率上調25個基點至4.75%，為連續第二次升息。30位經濟學家中有23位預期這項決定，其餘則預期升息50個基點。升幅不及市場中較鷹派人士的預期，披索因而下跌0.3%。

總裁Eli Remolona表示，8月27日會議仍可能再次升息，屆時將視數據考慮25或50個基點。不過，只要通膨預期仍受控，他認為漸進調整較為適當。菲律賓5月通膨降至6.8%，但仍遠高於2%至4%的目標區間；披索雖已從近期歷史低點回升，今年迄今仍貶值近3%。

兩項決策顯示，油價下跌無法促成一致的政策逆轉。兩個經濟體都受益於未來能源成本下降，但在本幣仍然脆弱、通膨實際值已走高之際，兩家央行都不能只依賴這項利多。印尼債券下跌與菲律賓披索走弱顯示，當地市場仍要求央行證明漸進升息足以應對壓力。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，日本5月通膨數據呈現同一問題的另一種樣貌。排除生鮮食品的核心消費者物價較一年前上漲1.4%，與前月相同且符合預期；排除生鮮食品與能源的通膨率為1.8%。政府補貼使汽油價格較一年前下跌7%，包括飯店住宿在內的服務成本則增強。

日本央行升息至1%後，這份數據並未動搖其漸進緊縮方向。日圓偏弱持續推高進口成本：5月平均匯率為1美元兌158.24日圓，東京週五上午約為161.31日圓。日本央行需要判斷的是，服務價格上升及企業間能源成本轉嫁能否持續到足以抵銷補貼帶來的整體通膨降溫。

## 中國擴大債券融資管道，拉丁美洲走勢分歧

隨著債券在信用供給中的占比升至歷史新高，中國持續演變的貨幣政策框架日益重要。5月政府與企業債券占未償信用總額30%。2025年新增債券融資首次超過新增貸款，差額約人民幣5,000億元；經濟學家預期2026年差距將進一步擴大。

這項轉變讓中國人民銀行不必反覆調降銀行放款基準，也能降低融資成本。銀行第1季淨息差降至歷史低點1.4%，限制其承受進一步降息的能力；與此同時，家庭支出、民間投資及貸款需求疲弱，使政策支持壓力升高。

中國人民銀行已透過公開市場操作注入流動性，讓一項政策性貸款利率降至歷史低點，並宣布縮窄銀行間隔夜融資利率走廊。央行計畫在例行7天期操作之外，新增隔夜逆回購操作。分析師預期，更窄且更低的利率走廊有助抑制盤中波動，並穩定市場對低成本短期流動性的預期，尤其是在月底。

流動性充裕促使中國債券最大持有者商業銀行增加買進。5年期公債殖利率已由1月的1.7%降至約1.5%；5年期AAA級公司債殖利率則由約9個月前的2.13%降至1.8%以下。這些水準遠低於3.5%的5年期貸款市場報價利率及3.1%的企業貸款平均利率。

2026年前5個月，企業債券融資增加人民幣1.7兆元，較去年同期高逾80%，新增貸款則減少11%。整體債券融資擴張有一部分來自北京以人民幣10兆元債券置換地方政府隱性債務的計畫，但變化並不限於公部門再融資：較低的市場殖利率正吸引企業借款人由銀行貸款轉向債券。

真正的限制在需求，而非能否取得低名目利率。債券管道可以降低融資成本，並讓中國人民銀行更能影響市場利率；但在信心與預期報酬仍疲弱時，光靠這項管道無法促使家庭或企業借款。野村經濟學家以流動性充裕及公債殖利率下降為由，將調降政策利率與存款準備率的預測延後至2027年。中國6月22日的貸款市場報價利率定價，將顯示官員是否繼續依靠市場流動性傳導，而非再度調降銀行放款基準。

拉丁美洲的政策方向各異。巴西央行已將Selic利率下調25個基點至14.25%，但週四市場反應顯示，投資人對央行提出的理由信心不足。巴西里爾下跌約1.3%，長天期交換利率上升約20個基點，因投資人聚焦於央行承認經濟成長與通膨均已加速。

官員主張，在將通膨回歸目標的評估期限延至2028年第1季後，降息仍屬適當。批評者則認為，這套理由與4.72%的年通膨率、具韌性的勞動市場、第1季1.1%的成長率，以及選舉年支撐消費的財政措施彼此矛盾。央行將2027年第4季通膨預測由3.5%上調至3.7%，促使部分經濟學家判斷降息循環可能已經結束，或會在8月停止。

智利則轉向限制性較低的政策立場。央行將政策利率維持在4.5%，立場轉為較中性，並把2026年成長預測區間由1.5%至2.5%下修為1%至1.75%。本週前三天，1年期交換利率下降11個基點至4.54%，當地銀行也開始預測年底前降息。

支持降息的理由包括消費與投資轉弱、通膨預期較受控制，以及5月消費者物價通膨為3.9%、更接近3%的目標。美國與伊朗達成初步協議時，央行已完成預測，因此油價大幅下跌可能帶來額外緩解。不過，市場對未來12個月降息機率的定價僅接近五成，反映投資人仍不確定經濟活動是否會充分轉弱、通膨是否會充分收斂，使央行有理由逆全球緊縮趨勢而行。

哥倫比亞債市在6月21日總統決選前，已開始反映政治變局。Pimco旗下基金5月淨買進6.7兆披索、約$20億的哥倫比亞國內公債，目前約持有外國投資人所持$430億債券的30%。哥倫比亞本幣債券近一個月報酬超過11%，為新興市場最佳；10年期殖利率則從5月中高點下降約2.5個百分點至12%以下。

這波漲勢始於保守派候選人Abelardo de la Espriella在首輪投票擊敗左派參議員Iván Cepeda。兩人在決選提出截然不同的財政與能源政策：Cepeda支持擴大社會計畫並繼續反對水力壓裂，De la Espriella則主張減稅、加強支出控制及提高民間投資。下屆政府將接手疲弱的經濟成長、擴大的財政赤字及加速的通膨，因此債市漲勢能否延續，不會只取決於選舉結果。

## 資本需求重塑公開與私募信貸

SpaceX正籌備一筆可能成為史上規模最大企業首發債之一的交易，銀行業者考慮發行至少$200億的投資級美元債。所得資金將用於再融資一筆2027年9月到期、規模$200億的臨時過橋貸款；這筆潛在交易也標誌著一項更龐大的融資挑戰才剛開始，資金需求涉及人工智慧、衛星及軌道資料中心。

SpaceX已完成首次公開募股，估值超過$2.5兆，並告知潛在股票投資人，這次IPO可能是公司最後一次發售股票。週四稍晚，三大信評機構均給予SpaceX投資級債券評等。管理層傾向透過更多舉債支應擴張，以免進一步稀釋股東權益。

預計所需資本規模極為龐大。高盛與Evercore ISI分析師估計，SpaceX到本世紀20年代末的支出可能超過$1兆。其中一項預測認為，2031年年度資本支出將超過$7,000億；Oppenheimer分析師則估計，屆時淨負債將超過$4,000億，遠高於近期約$130億。

債券投資人的報酬結構不同於股東。SpaceX目前尚未獲利，軌道資料中心的報酬規模及實現時點仍不確定；即使計畫表現超乎預期，債券持有人也無法分享票息以外的上行空間。Allspring美國投資級研究主管Jim Fitzpatrick認為，若SpaceX希望維持投資級評等，大部分支出最終仍需以股權融資。

這筆發行也將面對激烈的資本競爭。自去年11月以來，AI相關債券在多個信用市場的發行額已超過$3,000億。Anthropic與OpenAI可能進行大規模股權發行，既有科技公司也持續為資料中心、半導體及能源基礎設施融資。因此，SpaceX首發債不只考驗自身投資級評等可容納的負債規模，也將測試投資人願意在單一投資主題上承擔多少存續期間風險與集中度。

NextEra Energy顯示，這類融資需求已開始改變證券結構。這家公用事業公司本週發行3檔混合資本債，超越福斯汽車與BP，成為全球最大此類證券發行人。其中一檔期限40年，前20年不得贖回，遠長於一般5年或10年的不可贖回期；該檔獲得3檔債券中最多的認購訂單。

混合資本債屬次順位債務，可獲信評機構部分股權認定，使發行人能在不立即稀釋股東權益，也不必完全承擔發行優先債評等成本的情況下，為資本支出籌資。今年美元、歐元及英鎊混合資本債發行額已超過$730億，接近2023年同期的5倍。穆迪2024年調整評等方法後，更多美國企業得以進入這個市場。

對公用事業公司而言，這種結構可因應資料中心帶動的發電及電網容量投資急增。NextEra預期，截至2045年，美國電力需求增速將是此前20年的6倍；擬議收購Dominion Energy也會增加其融資需求。公司新發行的債券中，有兩檔成為本週交易最活絡的美國公司債。

投資人作出的讓步主要是接受較長的存續期間與次順位地位，卻未換得特別寬的估值溢價。混合資本債相對整體投資級市場的額外利差已收窄至56個基點，接近歷史最低。NextEra債券要等待20年才能首次贖回；若市場殖利率上升，或發行人認為再融資不具吸引力，持有人面臨的存續期間延長風險格外顯著。

評等較低的借款人則需提供明顯更高的讓利。Shutterfly以每$1面額98.2美分的價格發行$11.5億高收益債券，其中部分再融資債券的殖利率為12.5%。原定$5億的第一順位槓桿貸款轉由私募信貸機構承作後，Apollo將既有第二順位曝險轉入一筆新的$2.5億次順位級別，使自己的債權順位進一步後移。

這項交易用以因應Shutterfly總額$24億債務中接連到期的部位，也實質恢復了部分債權人的價值；這些債權人曾在2023年一項被穆迪與標普認定為困境債務交換的交易中蒙受損失。新債獲超額認購，之後交易價格也上升，但大幅讓利顯示投資人仍擔心高槓桿、季節性及AI可能造成的衝擊。

截至3月的3個月內，Shutterfly營收較一年前減少8%至$3.135億。公布的Ebitda為負$1,970萬，一年前則虧損$1,720萬；調整後Ebitda由虧損$150萬改善至約正$40萬。公司擁有$4.74億流動性及一筆尚未動用的循環額度，但高度仰賴第4季獲利抵銷前9個月的虧損。

Braskem的談判進度較慢。這家巴西石化生產商與新控股股東IG4 Capital，尚未取得啟動庭外重整所需的三分之一債權人支持。債權人反對期限較短的債券持有人取得較優條件及較小的隱含減記，待遇優於較長期限貸款的債權人；他們也質疑擬議抵押品、方案未提供債轉股選項，以及IG4與少數股東巴西石油公司不願注入新資本。

Braskem的方案包括延長到期日、降低票息及增加寬限期，但不包含股權出資或債務轉換。若7月前仍未取得門檻支持，尋求緊急法院保護的可能性將升高。眼前限制不在整體市場融資管道，而是資本結構中的公平待遇與贊助股東支持。

義大利網路服務商Eolo則尋求較傳統的私募解決方案。公司正與Apollo深入洽談約€5億融資，以再融資€3.75億高收益債券及€1.4億循環額度，兩者均於2028年到期。穆迪確認其B3評等，但指出公司槓桿偏高，且擴建網路需要資本支出。其債券報價約為每€1面額86歐分，因此私募方案較公開市場再融資更具吸引力。

儘管各筆交易條件差異很大，整體債券基金價格仍收高。LQD上漲0.28%，HYG上漲0.35%，JNK上漲0.34%，EMB上漲0.47%，顯示當日風險資產漲勢亦延伸至可交易信用債。擁有強勁股權估值或策略性資本計畫的投資級發行人，正嘗試運用發行規模與證券結構；受壓力的借款人若要延長到期日，仍須向貸款人提供殖利率、優先順位或贊助股東支持等讓利。

## 後續市場意義

依SIFMA假日建議，美國固定收益市場6月19日休市，下一次國內價格發現將延至6月22日。休市前，美債曲線所反映的7月升息押注接近五成，2年期殖利率仍高於4.18%，長天期債券則因實質殖利率下降與油運恢復而上漲。休市期間荷莫茲海峽的任何發展，都要等正常交易恢復後才會反映於美債。

能源市場接下來的考驗在實體供應，而非外交表態。近1,000萬桶油氣已開始運輸，但正常通行、產量及實際送達供應尚未恢復。就伊朗核計畫展開的60天談判期，也可能受到制裁、區域衝突及海峽控制權問題干擾。若船運持續且送達的燃料成本下降，將支持未來通膨走低；若供應再次中斷，Warsh首度主持會議後形成的曲線趨平將面臨挑戰。

中國將於6月22日上海時間09:00公布貸款市場報價利率。1年期利率目前為3.00%，5年期為3.50%，市場預期兩者均維持不變。在銀行息差受到壓縮之際，這項決定將顯示中國人民銀行是否繼續依賴較低的隔夜利率走廊、公開市場流動性及債券市場傳導，而不調降銀行放款基準。

加拿大同日美東時間08:30公布5月消費者物價。4月整體通膨為2.8%，市場預期升至3.0%。這是採用更新後商品籃的首次公布，數據組成對判斷能源成本轉嫁及加拿大央行政策路徑相當重要。

財政部休市後首批供給將於6月22日稍晚登場，包括$890億13週期國庫券及$770億26週期國庫券，兩者均於6月25日交割。需求分布將顯示，週四8週期國庫券承接較弱究竟是特定期限現象，還是前端現金需求已發生更廣泛變化。

附息債供給於6月23日開始，首先是$690億新發行2年期公債，於2028年6月30日到期。這是FOMC重新定價後，政策敏感期限面臨的首次直接初級市場考驗，當時投資人對7月會議的不確定性已大幅提高。財政部接著將於6月24日發行$700億新5年期公債，並於6月25日發行$440億新7年期公債，全部在6月30日交割。

澳洲將於6月24日雪梨時間11:30公布5月月度CPI。前次數據為月增0.4%、年增4.2%。結果將檢驗能源與服務通膨是否仍符合澳洲央行的限制性政策立場。

美國主要數據群將於6月25日美東時間08:30公布。初領失業救濟金數據將顯示，續領人數上升是否正轉變為更廣泛的勞動市場疲弱。耐久財訂單初值在前月上升7.9%後，預期下降5.0%；飛機訂單可能主導整體數字，核心資本財細項則能更清楚反映企業投資。

第1季GDP第3次估值預期顯示年化成長1.7%，第2次估值為1.6%。對利率更重要的是5月個人所得與支出：市場預期所得月增0.4%、支出月增0.6%、整體PCE價格月增0.5%、核心PCE價格月增0.3%。Warsh已將物價穩定置於政策反應的核心，這些通膨數據將決定7月升息押注是否仍合理，或重新後移至9月及更晚的會議。

墨西哥央行將於6月25日美東時間15:00公布利率決策。目前隔夜目標利率為6.50%，市場預期按兵不動。這項決定將檢驗能源通膨、披索對美元走強的敏感度，以及全球政策轉向緊縮，是否會使墨西哥降息循環繼續停擺。

哥倫比亞6月21日總統決選早於上述政策與數據事件。外資大舉流入當地債券，加上近一個月市場報酬超過11%，已使價格包含更多樂觀預期。最終勝選者的財政方案、能源政策與治理能力，將決定這波漲勢能否延續至選舉結果公布之後。

overall_summary.headline: 荷莫茲海峽恢復通行、長天期美債反彈，曲線前端仍反映聯準會鷹派重新定價
overall_summary.session_narrative:
載有近1,000萬桶石油或液化天然氣的船舶開始通過荷莫茲海峽，帶動前端以外的美債上漲。2年期殖利率小跌0.6個基點至4.18%，5年期下降3個基點至4.233%；10年期與30年期均下降3.4個基點，分別收在4.455%與4.899%。2年與10年期曲線再趨平2.8個基點至27.5個基點，顯示投資人保留對聯準會近期轉鷹的定價，同時認為能源前景改善與政策收緊更有利於長天期債券。

10年期美債上漲源於實質殖利率下降3.9個基點至2.181%，損益兩平通膨率反而上升0.5個基點至2.274%，因此這波走勢並不像名目殖利率下降本身所顯示的那麼偏向通膨降溫。初領失業救濟金人數降至22.6萬人，費城聯準銀行指數反彈至10.3，支付價格指數升至53.2；續領人數則增至181萬人。數據延續7月或9月升息的討論，但未引發美債再次全面拋售。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered beyond the policy-sensitive front end on June 18 as physical oil shipments began moving through the Strait of Hormuz, risk assets rallied and investors bought intermediate and long maturities after the Federal Reserve’s hawkish repricing. The 2-year yield edged down 0.6 basis point to 4.18%, retaining almost all of the previous session’s increase, while the 5-year fell 3 basis points to 4.233%. The 10- and 30-year yields each declined 3.4 basis points, to 4.455% and 4.899%.

The unequal rally extended the curve flattening created by Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as Fed chair. The 2s10s spread narrowed another 2.8 basis points to 27.5 basis points, leaving it 12.4 basis points flatter over the week, while 2s30s compressed to 71.9 basis points. The market continued to distinguish a sharply higher probability of near-term policy restraint from confidence that such restraint, together with lower prospective energy costs, could contain inflation farther out.

The composition of the 10-year move was less disinflationary than the decline in nominal yields alone suggested. The 10-year real yield fell 3.9 basis points to 2.181%, while the breakeven inflation rate increased 0.5 basis point to 2.274%. Thursday’s duration bid therefore came through lower inflation-adjusted yields rather than another fall in long-term inflation compensation. That contrasted with the previous month, over which the breakeven had declined 22.4 basis points while the real yield rose 9.1 basis points.

The change in the physical energy picture helped long Treasuries without producing a uniform daily fall in crude. Ships carrying nearly 10 million barrels of oil or liquefied natural gas had emerged from or entered the Strait of Hormuz after the US-Iran interim agreement took effect. WTI slipped 0.25% to $76.60, while Brent rose 0.38% to $79.85; both remained down more than 11% over the week and almost 29% over the month. Restored vessel traffic reduced the probability of a prolonged complete blockage, but the mixed daily close reflected the remaining uncertainty over how quickly normal volumes and damaged supply infrastructure can return.

US data did not invalidate the Fed’s inflation vigilance. Initial jobless claims fell to 226,000, close to expectations, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index rebounded to 10.3 and its prices-paid measure rose to 53.2. Continuing claims nevertheless increased to 1.810 million, keeping some labor-market softening in view. The combination was firm enough to sustain the market’s new debate over a July or September increase, but not strong enough to produce a second broad Treasury selloff.

Risk assets treated the reopening of Hormuz as the more immediate development. The S&P 500 gained 1.08%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 2.48% and the semiconductor index surged 6.42%, while the VIX fell 11.06% to 16.40. The dollar index climbed 0.76% as US rate expectations continued to move above those in several other economies, and gold futures fell 3.09% to $4,224.10. Investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt funds all advanced modestly. The close was consequently not a flight from risk: long Treasuries, equities and credit-fund prices rose together as investors separated relief over energy supply from the Fed’s more restrictive near-term reaction function.

## The Treasury Rebound Leaves the Front End on Alert

The recovery in Treasuries did little to reverse the central policy message embedded in the curve. Before Warsh’s debut, swaps assigned almost no probability to a July rate increase. By Thursday, the implied chance of a quarter-point move at the July 28-29 meeting was approaching one-half, and a full increase was priced by October. The 2-year yield’s small decline left it 11.7 basis points higher over the week, whereas the 10-year was slightly lower and the 30-year had fallen 5.7 basis points.

Trading in Fed funds futures showed that the repricing involved substantial new risk rather than only thin-market price movement. More than 500,000 contracts changed hands in the market segment used to express a July increase, roughly four times the 20-day average and a record. Open interest in August Fed funds futures rose by 67,000 contracts, equivalent to about 15% of the tenor’s outstanding positions. Because those contracts expire before the September meeting, the activity directly concentrated attention on July.

The market was also unwinding positions built around the prospect of rate cuts. Open interest in June 2026 Secured Overnight Financing Rate futures fell by 90,000 contracts. Total Fed funds futures open interest remained below its 1-year average, but the combination of fresh August positions and reduced dovish SOFR exposure showed that the response to Warsh extended beyond a one-session adjustment in cash Treasuries.

The new chair supplied no explicit timing for a move. His preference for less forward guidance instead makes each inflation, employment and activity release more consequential, particularly at the front end. The result can be a flatter curve even without an immediate increase: short maturities carry the risk that a strong monthly print pulls tightening forward, while long maturities can benefit if the market believes the Fed will act before inflation expectations become less stable.

Rob Kaplan, Goldman Sachs vice chairman and a former Dallas Fed president, reinforced that conditional interpretation. He said officials may need to increase rates in September or during the fall if inflation fails to cool before then. Kaplan also argued that policy changes rarely occur as isolated moves; a September increase could therefore be followed by one or two more. His qualification was important, however. He cautioned that the latest projections may not fully reflect the US-Iran agreement and the reopening of shipping routes, leaving scope for the inflation outlook to improve by the time the Fed updates its forecasts in September.

That tension was visible in Thursday’s economic releases. Initial unemployment claims declined by 4,000 to 226,000 in the week ended June 13, compared with an expected 225,000. The prior week was revised to 230,000 from 229,000. New layoffs therefore remained limited rather than showing the rapid deterioration that might force the Fed to disregard inflation.

The less favorable labor evidence appeared in the measures of persistence. The four-week average of initial claims rose to 223,250 from a revised 219,250, its highest level since December, while continuing claims increased by 24,000 to 1.810 million in the week ended June 6. The previous continuing-claims figure was revised to 1.786 million from 1.795 million. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%. Hiring and re-employment may be becoming more difficult even though the latest flow of new claims remains low.

Manufacturing provided a firmer growth signal with an uncomfortable cost component. The Philadelphia Fed’s general-activity index rebounded to 10.3 in June from minus 0.4, slightly above the 9.8-to-10.0 range of expectations. New orders jumped to 27.3 from minus 1.7, shipments rose to 14.9 from 4.9 and employment returned to positive territory at 7.9 from minus 2.8. The breadth across orders, output and jobs made the recovery more substantial than a headline-index bounce.

Price pressure strengthened at the same time. The prices-paid index rose to 53.2 from 47.9, even as prices received declined to 20.3 from 26.3. Manufacturers remained optimistic: the future general-activity index was 50.2, only modestly below 53.2, and expected capital expenditure increased to 41.2 from 30.9. The release thus supported a growth-plus-input-cost reading rather than a straightforward disinflation signal.

Treasury supply added a separate test of the real-rate structure. The $24 billion reopening of 5-year inflation-protected securities stopped at a 1.955% real yield, sharply above the 1.367% result at April’s $26 billion new issue. The bid-to-cover ratio improved to 2.61 from 2.57. Indirect bidders took 68.59% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders received 27.99% and primary dealers were left with only 3.43%, down from 8.48% in April.

The auction’s larger real-yield stop primarily reflected the substantial change in market levels since April. The demand statistics nevertheless showed that investors absorbed the reopening with slightly stronger cover and a larger combined end-user share. The securities, carrying a 1.250% coupon and maturing April 15, 2031, settle June 30.

Cash-market activity around inflation-protected debt was unusually heavy. FINRA recorded $47.8 billion of TIPS par activity, 114.3% more than the prior session. Activity in TIPS with no more than 5 years remaining increased 130.1% to $31.3 billion, with an on-the-run share of 69.3%. Those figures do not identify the direction of investor transactions, but the concentration around the auction sector confirmed that the reopening occurred during a marked increase in market engagement.

The bill auctions were more divided. Treasury’s $70 billion 4-week sale stopped at 3.580%, down from 3.595% a week earlier. Cover declined to 2.99 from 3.13, but indirect participation increased to 72.30% and the dealer share fell to 24.46%. The $75 billion 8-week auction stopped higher at 3.640%, versus 3.610% previously, as cover dropped to 2.57 from 2.94. Indirect participation fell to 51.49% and dealers absorbed 44.56%, compared with 28.14% at the prior sale. Both settle June 23, but the softer 8-week allocation showed that front-end cash demand was not uniform across neighboring maturities.

## Britain Holds as Global Policy Paths Diverge

The Bank of England held its policy rate at 3.75%, but a 7-2 vote preserved a meaningful tightening risk even after the sharp retreat in oil. Chief Economist Huw Pill and external member Megan Greene favored an immediate quarter-point increase to 4%. In April, Pill had been the sole dissenter, so the expansion of the hawkish minority mattered even as the majority chose to wait.

The bank lowered its forecast for peak inflation in Q4 to 3.25% from 3.6%, acknowledging the improvement in prospective energy costs. Oil had fallen below $80 a barrel from a wartime peak of $108, and May consumer-price inflation had come in at 2.8%, below the bank’s 3.3% forecast. Officials also judged that weakness in demand and the labor market would limit second-round effects.

The domestic activity evidence supported patience. The UK had lost 64,000 jobs since the Iran war began in February, regular private-sector pay growth had slowed to its weakest pace in 5 years and GDP contracted 0.1% in April. The BOE estimated underlying growth at only 0.2% in Q1 and expected a similar pace in Q2. Most Monetary Policy Committee members judged that the tightening in financial conditions since the conflict began already provided some insurance against inflation.

The hold was not a declaration that the energy shock had passed. Governor Andrew Bailey said falling oil was encouraging but warned that prices remained above prewar levels and that the damage to Middle Eastern infrastructure still had to be assessed. The majority said its response should be robust if price pressure strengthened, while Greene argued for insurance against larger second-round effects until there was evidence they were not materializing.

Markets marginally reduced expectations for further BOE tightening but continued to price one full quarter-point increase this year and roughly a 30% probability of a second. Sterling fell about 0.5% against the dollar to $1.3225, its weakest level since early April. The reaction reflected both the lower inflation forecast and the widening US policy differential after Warsh’s debut.

The euro area retained a more explicit tightening debate. ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane said the upper end of the estimated neutral-rate range had risen to 2.5% from 2.25%. With the deposit rate at 2.25% following the June 11 increase, that assessment implies that another quarter-point move would not necessarily push policy clearly into restrictive territory.

Lane described the Middle East episode as a medium-sized shock with a medium degree of persistence, smaller than the disruption following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine but still capable of keeping inflation above target for a prolonged period. Even as oil declines, he expects the accumulated energy shock to lift food, goods and services prices.

Other ECB officials supplied evidence that this pass-through was already broadening. Jose Luis Escrivá said energy costs were appearing in core inflation, particularly services, transportation and food. He emphasized that wage second-round effects had not materialized, but that their absence could not yet be assumed to persist. Martin Kocher likewise said consumer prices would remain elevated for some time despite the interim peace agreement and that the ECB remained prepared to act.

Spain illustrated the regional pressure. The Bank of Spain raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.6%, 0.6 percentage point above its March projection, citing energy, non-energy industrial goods, services and partial pass-through from higher fuel costs. Its 2027 forecast increased slightly to 2.6%. Growth projections remained much stronger than those for the broader euro area, at 2.3% this year and 1.7% next year, leaving Spain with both firmer activity and more persistent inflation.

Asian central banks confronted a more immediate combination of currency depreciation and imported inflation. Bank Indonesia increased its BI-Rate by 25 basis points to 5.75%, its third rise in about a month and the latest step in 100 basis points of tightening this year. Governor Perry Warjiyo said the bank would continue to act aggressively in support of the rupiah.

The currency closed 0.2% stronger after the decision, while Indonesia’s 10-year government-bond yield rose 15 basis points, its largest increase in more than a week. Beginning in July, foreign-currency transactions of at least $10,000 will require an underlying transaction, down from a $100,000 threshold earlier in the year. Bank Indonesia estimates the rule will lift the share of foreign-exchange transactions supported by underlying documentation to 98.1%.

The tightening was motivated more by the exchange rate and capital flows than by current headline inflation, which is expected to remain within the bank’s 1.5%-3.5% target range. Food and energy costs, possible El Niño disruption and the lagged effect of rupiah weakness nevertheless leave upside risks. The prospect of Fed increases compounds the pressure by making dollar assets more competitive and increasing the cost of stabilizing the currency.

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas also raised its target reverse-repurchase rate by 25 basis points, to 4.75%, the second consecutive increase. Twenty-three of 30 economists had expected that move, while the remainder anticipated 50 basis points. The peso slipped 0.3% after the smaller increment disappointed the more hawkish part of the market.

Governor Eli Remolona said another increase remained possible at the August 27 meeting and that either 25 or 50 basis points could be considered depending on the data. He nevertheless described gradual steps as appropriate while inflation expectations remain anchored. Philippine inflation eased to 6.8% in May but remained far above the 2%-4% target range, and the peso was still almost 3% weaker for the year despite recovering from its recent record low.

The two decisions showed why lower oil cannot produce a uniform policy reversal. Both economies benefit from cheaper prospective energy, but neither central bank can rely on that alone while its currency remains vulnerable and realized inflation has already risen. Indonesia’s bond selloff and the Philippine peso’s decline showed that local markets continued to demand evidence that incremental tightening would be sufficient.

After the US fixed-income close, Japan’s May inflation figures offered a different version of the same issue. Core consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 1.4% from a year earlier, unchanged from the prior month and in line with expectations. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy was 1.8%. Government subsidies helped gasoline prices fall 7% from a year earlier, while services costs, including hotel accommodation, strengthened.

The release did not challenge the Bank of Japan’s gradual tightening direction after its increase to 1%. A weak yen—averaging 158.24 per dollar in May and trading around 161.31 on Friday morning in Tokyo—continues to lift import costs. The distinction for the BOJ is whether rising services prices and business-to-business energy pass-through become durable enough to outweigh the subsidy-induced moderation in the headline measures.

## China Expands the Bond Channel as Latin America Splits

China’s evolving monetary framework is increasingly important because bonds now supply a record share of credit. Government and corporate securities accounted for 30% of outstanding credit in May. New bond financing surpassed new loans for the first time in 2025, by about 500 billion yuan, and economists expect the gap to widen in 2026.

The shift gives the People’s Bank of China a route to lower borrowing costs without repeatedly reducing bank lending benchmarks. Banks’ net interest margins fell to a record-low 1.4% in Q1, limiting their capacity to absorb further reductions in loan rates. At the same time, weak household spending, private investment and loan demand are increasing pressure for support.

The PBOC has responded by injecting liquidity through open-market operations, allowing a policy-loan rate to fall to a record and announcing a narrower corridor for overnight interbank funding. It plans to add overnight reverse-repurchase operations to its regular 7-day transactions. Analysts expect the narrower and lower corridor to curb intraday volatility and anchor expectations for inexpensive short-term liquidity, particularly around month-end.

That liquidity has encouraged commercial banks—the largest holders of Chinese bonds—to increase purchases. Five-year government yields have declined to about 1.5% from 1.7% in January, while yields on 5-year AAA corporate debt have fallen below 1.8% from 2.13% roughly 9 months earlier. Those levels are far below the 5-year loan prime rate of 3.5% and the average corporate loan rate of 3.1%.

Corporate bond financing increased by 1.7 trillion yuan in the first 5 months of 2026, more than 80% above the same period last year, while new loans declined 11%. Part of the broader bond expansion reflects Beijing’s 10-trillion-yuan program to replace hidden local-government liabilities with securities. The change nevertheless extends beyond public-sector refinancing: cheaper market yields are drawing corporate borrowers away from bank loans.

The limitation is demand rather than access to low nominal rates. The bond channel can reduce financing costs and give the PBOC more influence over market rates, but it cannot by itself induce households or firms to borrow when confidence and expected returns remain weak. Nomura economists have pushed their forecasts for reductions in the policy rate and reserve-requirement ratio into 2027, citing abundant liquidity and falling government-bond yields. China’s June 22 loan-prime-rate fixing will show whether officials continue to rely on market-liquidity transmission instead of another reduction in bank benchmarks.

Latin America moved in several directions. Brazil’s central bank had lowered the Selic rate by 25 basis points to 14.25%, but Thursday’s market response showed how little confidence investors placed in the accompanying explanation. The real fell about 1.3% and long-dated swap rates rose around 20 basis points as investors focused on the bank’s acknowledgement that growth and inflation had accelerated.

Officials argued that a reduction was appropriate while extending the relevant horizon for returning inflation to target into Q1 2028. Critics saw tension between that justification and annual inflation of 4.72%, a resilient labor market, 1.1% Q1 growth and election-year fiscal measures supporting consumption. The central bank raised its Q4 2027 inflation forecast to 3.7% from 3.5%, prompting some economists to conclude that the easing cycle may already be finished or could stop in August.

Chile, by contrast, moved toward a less restrictive bias. Its central bank held the policy rate at 4.5%, shifted to a more neutral stance and reduced its 2026 growth projection to a range of 1%-1.75% from 1.5%-2.5%. One-year swaps fell 11 basis points over the first three days of the week to 4.54%, and local banks began forecasting a reduction before year-end.

The case rests on weaker consumption and investment, more contained inflation expectations and May consumer inflation of 3.9%, closer to the 3% target. The preliminary US-Iran accord was reached after the bank prepared its forecasts, so the large decline in oil may provide additional relief. Yet market pricing was only near an even chance of a cut over 12 months, reflecting uncertainty over whether activity will weaken enough and inflation converge far enough to justify moving against the wider global tightening trend.

Colombia’s bond market was already pricing a political change before the June 21 presidential runoff. Pimco funds bought a net 6.7 trillion pesos, about $2 billion, of domestic government bonds in May and now hold roughly 30% of the $43 billion owned by foreign investors. Colombian local debt returned more than 11% over the past month, the best performance among emerging markets, while the 10-year yield fell about 2.5 percentage points from its mid-May peak to below 12%.

The rally followed conservative candidate Abelardo de la Espriella’s first-round victory over left-wing Senator Iván Cepeda. Their runoff presents sharply different fiscal and energy policies: Cepeda favors expanded social programs and continued opposition to fracking, while De la Espriella has proposed tax cuts, tighter expenditure control and measures to increase private investment. The next administration will inherit weak growth, a widening fiscal deficit and accelerating inflation, leaving the bond rally dependent on more than the election result alone.

## Capital Needs Reshape Public and Private Credit

SpaceX is preparing what could become one of the largest corporate bond debuts on record, with bankers considering an investment-grade dollar offering of at least $20 billion. The proceeds would refinance a temporary $20 billion bridge loan maturing in September 2027, but the prospective transaction also marks the beginning of a far larger financing challenge tied to artificial intelligence, satellites and orbital data centers.

The company completed its initial public offering with a valuation above $2.5 trillion and told prospective equity investors that the IPO could be its last stock sale. Late Thursday, all three major rating firms assigned SpaceX investment-grade bond ratings. Management’s preference is to fund more of the expansion through debt rather than dilute shareholders further.

The projected capital requirement is extraordinary. Goldman Sachs and Evercore ISI analysts estimate SpaceX could spend more than $1 trillion by the end of the decade. One projection places annual capital expenditure above $700 billion by 2031, while Oppenheimer analysts model more than $400 billion of net debt by then, up from about $13 billion recently.

Bond investors face a different payoff structure from equity holders. SpaceX is not profitable, the scale and timing of returns from orbital data centers remain uncertain, and debt offers no participation beyond its coupon if the projects exceed expectations. Jim Fitzpatrick, Allspring’s head of US investment-grade research, argued that most of the expenditure would ultimately need equity financing if SpaceX is to preserve investment-grade ratings.

The offering would also arrive amid intense competition for capital. AI-linked debt issuance has exceeded $300 billion since November across several credit markets. Anthropic and OpenAI may seek large equity offerings, while established technology companies continue to finance data centers, semiconductors and energy infrastructure. SpaceX’s debut therefore tests not only its own rating capacity but the amount of duration and concentration investors will accept from a single investment theme.

NextEra Energy illustrates how that financing demand is already changing security structures. The utility sold three hybrid bonds during the week and overtook Volkswagen and BP as the world’s largest issuer of the securities. One tranche has a 40-year maturity and cannot be called for 20 years, far longer than the conventional 5- or 10-year non-call period. It attracted the most orders of the three tranches.

Hybrids are subordinated obligations that receive partial equity treatment from rating firms, allowing issuers to finance capital spending without immediately diluting shareholders or taking the full ratings cost of senior debt. Dollar, euro and sterling hybrid issuance has exceeded $73 billion this year, almost five times the comparable 2023 volume. A 2024 change in Moody’s methodology helped open the market to more US companies.

For utilities, the structure addresses rapidly rising investment in generation and grid capacity for data centers. NextEra expects the growth rate of US power demand through 2045 to be six times that of the preceding 20 years, and its proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy would add to its financing needs. Two of its new tranches became the most actively traded US corporate bonds of the week.

The concession to investors is duration and subordination rather than an especially wide valuation premium. The additional spread on hybrids over the broader investment-grade market has narrowed to 56 basis points, close to its tightest level on record. The 20-year wait for NextEra’s first call leaves holders unusually exposed if market yields rise or the issuer finds refinancing unattractive.

Lower-rated borrowers were paying much more explicit concessions. Shutterfly sold $1.15 billion of high-yield bonds at 98.2 cents on the dollar, with part of the refinancing offering a 12.5% yield. Apollo rolled its existing second-lien exposure into a new $250 million junior tranche, subordinating its own claim further, after the planned $500 million first-lien leveraged loan was shifted toward a private-credit lender.

The transaction addressed a rapid sequence of maturities within Shutterfly’s $2.4 billion debt load. It also effectively restored value to creditors who took losses in a 2023 exchange classified by Moody’s and S&P as distressed. The new bonds were oversubscribed and subsequently traded higher, but the concessions showed that investors remained concerned about high leverage, seasonality and possible AI-driven disruption.

Revenue declined 8% from a year earlier to $313.5 million in the 3 months through March. Reported Ebitda was negative $19.7 million, compared with a $17.2 million loss a year earlier, though adjusted Ebitda improved to about $400,000 from a $1.5 million loss. Shutterfly had $474 million of liquidity and an undrawn revolving facility, but depends heavily on Q4 earnings to offset losses during the first 9 months of the year.

Braskem’s negotiations were less advanced. The Brazilian petrochemical producer and new controlling shareholder IG4 Capital had not secured the support of one-third of creditors needed to begin an out-of-court restructuring. Creditors objected that shorter-dated bondholders would receive better terms and smaller implicit haircuts than lenders in longer facilities. They also challenged the proposed collateral, the absence of a debt-for-equity option and the unwillingness of IG4 and minority shareholder Petrobras to inject new capital.

Braskem’s plan includes maturity extensions, lower coupons and additional grace periods but no equity contribution or debt conversion. Failure to obtain the threshold support by July would increase the likelihood of emergency court protection. The dispute leaves capital-structure equality and sponsor support, rather than broad market access, as the immediate constraints.

Italian internet provider Eolo was pursuing a more conventional private solution. It entered advanced talks with Apollo for roughly €500 million to refinance €375 million of high-yield bonds and a €140 million revolving facility, both due in 2028. Moody’s affirmed the company’s B3 rating while citing high leverage and the capital expenditure required to expand its network. Its bonds were quoted around 86 cents on the euro, helping explain the appeal of a private package over a public refinancing.

Broad bond-fund prices nevertheless finished higher. LQD gained 0.28%, HYG 0.35%, JNK 0.34% and EMB 0.47%. Those moves showed that the day’s risk rally extended into traded credit, even as individual transactions demanded sharply different protections. Investment-grade issuers with strong equity valuations or strategic capital programs were experimenting with scale and structure; stressed borrowers were still giving lenders yield, seniority or sponsor concessions to extend maturities.

## Forward Market Significance

US fixed-income markets are closed on June 19 under the SIFMA holiday recommendation, shifting the next domestic price discovery to June 22. The interruption matters because the Treasury curve enters the break with July tightening wagers near a coin flip, a 2-year yield still above 4.18% and long maturities rallying on a combination of lower real yields and restored oil traffic. Developments in Hormuz during the closure will reach Treasuries only when regular trading resumes.

The energy test is now physical rather than diplomatic. Nearly 10 million barrels had begun moving, but normal passage, production and delivered supply have not yet been restored. The 60-day negotiating period over Iran’s nuclear program also remains vulnerable to interruptions involving sanctions, regional conflict and control of the strait. Sustained vessel traffic and lower delivered fuel costs would support the decline in prospective inflation; renewed disruption would challenge the flattening that followed Warsh’s debut.

China’s loan prime rates are fixed June 22 at 09:00 in Shanghai. The 1-year rate stands at 3.00% and the 5-year rate at 3.50%, with both expected to remain unchanged. The decision will indicate whether the PBOC continues to rely on its lower overnight corridor, open-market liquidity and bond-market transmission rather than reducing bank lending benchmarks while margins are compressed.

Canada releases May consumer prices at 08:30 ET the same day. Headline inflation was 2.8% in April and is expected to rise to 3.0%. It is the first release using an updated basket, making the composition important for judging energy pass-through and the Bank of Canada’s policy path.

Treasury’s first post-holiday supply arrives later June 22 with $89 billion of 13-week bills and $77 billion of 26-week bills, both settling June 25. Their demand profiles will show whether the weaker absorption at Thursday’s 8-week auction was maturity-specific or part of a broader change in front-end cash demand.

Coupon supply begins June 23 with a $69 billion new 2-year note maturing June 30, 2028. The auction is the first direct primary-market test of policy-sensitive duration since the FOMC repricing and comes while investors are carrying substantially more uncertainty around the July meeting. Treasury follows with a $70 billion new 5-year note on June 24 and a $44 billion new 7-year note on June 25, all settling June 30.

Australia’s May monthly CPI is released June 24 at 11:30 in Sydney. The previous readings were a 0.4% monthly increase and 4.2% inflation from a year earlier. The result will test whether energy and services inflation remain consistent with the Reserve Bank of Australia’s restrictive stance.

The principal US data cluster arrives June 25 at 08:30 ET. Initial claims will show whether the rise in continuing claims is becoming broader labor-market weakness. Advance durable-goods orders are expected to fall 5.0% after a 7.9% increase, with aircraft likely to dominate the headline, while the core capital-goods details will provide a cleaner view of business investment.

The third estimate of Q1 GDP is expected to show 1.7% annualized growth, compared with 1.6% in the second estimate. More consequential for rates will be May personal income and outlays. Expectations call for income to rise 0.4%, spending 0.6%, headline PCE prices 0.5% and core PCE prices 0.3% on the month. After Warsh placed price stability at the center of the reaction function, those inflation readings will determine whether the market’s July wagers remain plausible or shift back toward September and later meetings.

Banco de Mexico decides at 15:00 ET on June 25. The overnight target stands at 6.50%, and the expected outcome is a hold. The decision will test whether energy inflation, peso sensitivity to the stronger dollar and the wider turn toward global tightening keep Mexico’s easing cycle closed.

Colombia’s June 21 presidential runoff precedes those policy and data events. The large foreign inflow into local bonds and the market’s more than 11% monthly return have increased the amount of optimism embedded in prices. The fiscal program, energy policy and governability of the eventual winner will determine whether that rally can survive beyond the election result.

overall_summary.headline: Long Treasuries rebound as Hormuz traffic resumes, while the front end retains the Fed’s hawkish repricing
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied beyond the front end as nearly 10 million barrels of oil or liquefied natural gas began moving through the Strait of Hormuz. The 2-year yield slipped 0.6 basis point to 4.18%, while the 5-year fell 3 basis points to 4.233% and the 10- and 30-year yields each declined 3.4 basis points, to 4.455% and 4.899%. The 2s10s curve flattened another 2.8 basis points to 27.5 basis points as investors retained the Fed’s hawkish near-term repricing but gave longer maturities more credit for prospective energy relief and policy restraint.

The 10-year rally came through a 3.9-basis-point decline in the real yield to 2.181%, while the breakeven inflation rate rose 0.5 basis point to 2.274%, making the move less disinflationary than the nominal decline alone suggested. Initial claims fell to 226,000 and the Philadelphia Fed index rebounded to 10.3, with prices paid rising to 53.2, although continuing claims increased to 1.810 million. The data sustained debate over a July or September increase without causing another broad Treasury selloff.

The reopening relief also lifted equities and credit funds and pushed volatility lower, confirming that the Treasury rally was not a flight from risk. Oil closed mixed on the day but remained down more than 11% over the week, while the dollar strengthened as US rate expectations moved above those in several other economies. The remaining test is whether vessel traffic, production and delivered supply normalize enough to validate the market’s improved inflation outlook.
